chunks: And in it that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, did not create anything except that it is within His power.
And He did not grant His servants in anything of His creation a power over anything other than what He had decreed for them.
So whoever claims that he has power over something with a power other than the power of Allah for it, then he is a disbeliever.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for being a disbeliever regarding divine power?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this doctrine to counter the Ghulat (extremists) who attributed independent creative power to the Imams, thereby affirming the Imams' status as perfect servants rather than co-creators. This distinction preserves the principle of *Tawhid* (Divine Oneness) by clarifying that all authority, including that of the Prophet and Imams, is derived and contingent upon Allah's decree.
